messages:
marie: Thanks again for the thoughtful questions in the all-hands. Quick follow-up on runway, spend controls, and procurement — wanted to put clarity here so teams can act quickly.

alex: Appreciate this — can you confirm runway number again (months at current burn)?

marie: Sure — at current net burn we're at ~22 months of runway. That accounts for committed hires and Q2 infrastructure spend. Noting that Dedicated customers ramp could change short-term.

jamal: Question on approval thresholds: what needs exec signoff vs. manager? Example: $40k infra spend.

marie: Good call. Updated thresholds: manager approval up to $5k, director up to $25k, finance+director for $25k-$100k, exec review for >$100k. Procurement exceptions for multi-year deals escalate earlier. I'll post the table in the finance doc.

lara: Where's the canonical doc? I want to share with PMs.

marie: Link: https://redwood.company/ops/procurement — see "Approval matrix" and "Vendor onboarding". Use the request template under "Forms".

sophie: For committed infra (GPUs) purchases, is that treated as CapEx or OpEx? Tax folks asked.

marie: Short answer: we treat long-term hardware purchases as CapEx if owned; cloud reserved capacity / committed spend is OpEx. Finance will annotate vendor invoices accordingly. If you're unsure, tag finance in the PR.

jamal: For exceptions (we have a vendor renewal at $60k fast) who do I ping?

marie: Ping me and @finance-bot. Please include: vendor name, SOW, renewal term, and expected ROI/impact. For urgent renewals we can fast-track approval within 48 hours if docs are complete.

finance-bot: Action created: PROC-4932 (vendor renewal fast-track). Assignee: jamal. Deadline: 48 hours.

alex: Are we changing spend freezes or hiring pause rules?

marie: No broad freezes. We are tightening discretionary spend: travel, swag, conferences — teams should get manager signoff and include a brief business justification. We still approve headcount hires per previously shared hiring rubric.

lara: Any update on automation for PO routing? Manual is slowing us down.

marie: Yes — procurement is rolling a PO workflow next week (Pilot: eng infra + product). Quick snippet of approval flow we're testing:
```
request -> manager -> procurement -> finance (auto-tag) -> director (if >25k)
```
Expect a short rollout email with links to the pilot form.

jamal: Will the PO tool integrate with Confluence/vendor docs?

marie: Initial pilot stores attachments in the procurement drive and links in Confluence pages. Longer-term we'll integrate with our contract repo.

sophie: Action items I heard?

marie: 1) Finance posts updated approval matrix in the doc by EOD Wednesday. 2) Procurement PO pilot starts next week; pilot invite to infra/product. 3) For urgent renewals, submit to PROC-4932 and tag @finance-bot. 4) Finance to label CapEx vs OpEx on invoices when requested.

lara: Thanks — I'll forward to PM guild. :thumbsup:

jamal: Sending PROC-4932 details now.

marie: Thanks everyone. If you want a quick sync, I'm available tomorrow 11–11:30 for a 15 min Q&A.

alex: Thanks Marie, this helps a lot.

finance-bot: Note: document updated at https://redwood.company/ops/procurement (approval matrix v1.2).
